question.prompt: An ATM password at Fred’s Bank is composed of four digits from \(0\) to \(9,\) with repeated digits allowable. If no password may begin with the sequence \(9,\) \(1,\) \(1,\) then how many passwords are possible?

solutions.explanation:
A password is a string of four digits, so \(0\) is allowed in the first position. Each position has \(10\) choices, with repetitions allowed. Thus there are

\[10\cdot10\cdot10\cdot10=10{,}000\]

strings before applying the restriction. Each is counted exactly once by its four digits.

A forbidden password has its first three digits fixed as \(911\), while its fourth digit has \(10\) choices. These are precisely \(9110\) through \(9119\). Removing those ten strings leaves every allowed password exactly once, giving

\[10{,}000-10=\boxed{9{,}990},\]

choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
solutions.title: Subtract the forbidden passwords
